chains.title: Alt allele creates a GATA3-responsive LMO1 enhancer
chains.element: The variant lies in a cis-regulatory element that acts as an enhancer.

links.claim: GATA3 is the leading TF candidate; alt A corresponds to T on the opposite strand, the allele reported to create a GATA3-binding site. No QBiC-SELEX result is supplied here.
Greater GATA3 binding at alt A increases activity of the variant-containing enhancer.
This effect occurs in neuroblastoma cells such as SK-N-SH, where LMO1 can contribute to tumor biology.
Increased LMO1 expression raises neuroblastoma susceptibility.

predictions: An alt-A enhancer reporter has greater activity than a ref-C reporter in SK-N-SH cells.
Changing alt A to ref C reduces LMO1 expression; reducing GATA3 should weaken the allelic difference.
falsified_if: Matched ref-C and alt-A reporters show no reproducible activity difference.
Editing alt A to ref C does not reduce LMO1 expression in an appropriate neuroblastoma model.

chains.title: Null: no TF-mediated effect of this variant
predictions: Ref-C and alt-A constructs show no reproducible difference in enhancer activity.
Editing this base does not produce a consistent change in LMO1 expression; any association could reflect linkage or another cause.
falsified_if: A reproducible allele-dependent effect is observed in an appropriate cellular assay and is linked to TF occupancy or perturbation.

chains.title: GATA3 binding represses the LMO1 enhancer
chains.element: The variant-containing element is a GATA3-responsive enhancer whose activity is repressed by GATA3.

links.claim: GATA3 is the candidate TF, and alt A is predicted to bind it more strongly based on the reported allele-specific binding-site interpretation; no QBiC-SELEX result is supplied here.
Greater GATA3 binding at alt A represses the variant-containing element.
Repression of the element reduces LMO1 expression.
The effect occurs in neuroblastoma cells in which GATA3 and LMO1 are expressed.
Reduced LMO1 expression lowers neuroblastoma susceptibility.

predictions: An alt-A enhancer reporter has lower activity than a ref-C reporter in SK-N-SH cells.
Changing ref C to alt A increases GATA3 occupancy but reduces LMO1 expression.
falsified_if: The alt-A reporter is more active than the ref-C reporter.
GATA3 depletion fails to change the allelic expression effect despite confirmed GATA3 expression.

chains.title: A related GATA factor, rather than GATA3, activates LMO1
chains.element: The variant-containing element is an enhancer responsive to GATA2.

links.claim: GATA2 is a speculative alternative because it is related to GATA3; alt A is hypothesized to bind it more strongly from the proposed GATA motif change. No GATA2-specific QBiC-SELEX result is supplied here.
Greater GATA2 binding at alt A increases enhancer activity.
The effect occurs in neuroblastoma cells that express GATA2 and LMO1.
Increased LMO1 expression raises neuroblastoma susceptibility.

predictions: The alt-A enhancer reporter is more active than the ref-C reporter.
GATA2 perturbation changes the allelic effect more than GATA3 perturbation does.
falsified_if: GATA2 is not expressed in the relevant cells or does not occupy the element.
GATA2 perturbation has no effect on the allelic enhancer or LMO1 expression difference.

matrix.test: Matched ref-C versus alt-A enhancer reporter in SK-N-SH cells

outcomes.outcome: Alt-A reporter activity is higher than ref-C.
Alt-A reporter activity is lower than ref-C.
Alt-A reporter activity is higher than ref-C.

matrix.test: Isogenic editing of the variant followed by LMO1 expression measurement in SK-N-SH

outcomes.outcome: A-to-C editing reduces LMO1 expression, with the effect dependent on GATA2.
Editing has no consistent effect on LMO1 expression.

matrix.test: Compare GATA3 and GATA2 occupancy and perturbation effects at the element

outcomes.outcome: GATA3 occupancy or perturbation tracks the alt-A effect more strongly than GATA2.
GATA3 occupancy tracks the effect, while its perturbation supports repression.
GATA2 occupancy or perturbation tracks the alt-A effect more strongly than GATA3.
No convincing allele-dependent occupancy or perturbation effect.

next_experiment: Run a matched ref-C versus alt-A enhancer reporter assay in SK-N-SH cells. It is the cheapest proposed test of the top two chains: H1 predicts higher alt-A activity, whereas the null predicts no reproducible difference. A reporter result would not by itself establish endogenous chromatin effects or identify the responsible TF.
